prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one 4:3 landscape painting for The Burnt Book Sanskrit learning story. Request 1536 x 1152 native output or the closest supported native 4:3 resolution. Refined Indian watercolor with restrained gouache on warm ivory paper; organic detail, quiet ochre, sage, dusty terracotta, muted indigo. Warm, gentle, evocative storytelling, consistent character design.
Canonical scene brief: The last library shelf with small mist figures of a father, a mother, a brother and a giver holding out his hands; the ink-stained spirit hopping onto the shelf and waving its pen; Śuka murmuring family words like a lullaby; Dādī listening.
Character appearances:
you: Always seen from behind or at a distance, face never detailed, so every learner can be the hero: a young person in a simple ochre kurta with a cloth shoulder bag.
dadi: A warm, sharp-eyed grandmother in her seventies, silver hair in a low bun, round spectacles, a cream cotton sari with a thin maroon border and a grey shawl; carries a cloth-bound notebook.
shuka: A bright green rose-ringed parrot with a red beak and a faint pink and black neck ring, a little scruffy, very expressive eyes; usually on your shoulder or Dādī's.
acarya: A very old, serene scholar with a white beard and a saffron shawl, a palm-leaf manuscript always under his arm, kind half-closed eyes.
kavika: A small blue-black spirit with ink-stained wisps, a reed pen behind one ear.
Phone-first composition: clear compact narrative grouping, essential faces, hands and objects comfortably inside all edges. Show the complete scene without border. No collage or multi-panel layout.
MANDATORY TEXT OVERRIDE: this card authorizes NO writing in the painting. Where the scene brief or character description mentions letters, a register, script, writing, numbers, sacred symbols or letter-shaped objects, show the corresponding physical door, pillar, book, leaf, crown or cord WITHOUT any letters or letterlike marks. Use purely floral carvings and completely blank smooth manuscript surfaces. Teaching letters remain separate live app text. No typography, numerals, Om signs, invented script, explanatory marks, sound lines, watermark or labels anywhere.

image.brief: The last library shelf with small mist figures of a father, a mother, a brother and a giver holding out his hands; the ink-stained spirit hopping onto the shelf and waving its pen; Śuka murmuring family words like a lullaby; Dādī listening.

alt.en: A shelf of mist figures of kin, a father, a mother, a brother and a giver
alt.hi: अलमारी पर नातों की धुंध-आकृतियाँ: पिता, माता, भाई और दाता

narration.en: The last shelf holds the words of kin: father, mother, brother, giver. The ink-stained spirit hops onto it and waves his pen. “These end in {{ऋ}},” says Dādī. “The vowel that is almost an r. Where it can, it turns into {{अर्}}; elsewhere into {{र्}}.” Śuka mutters “पिता, माता, भ्राता” as though trying out a lullaby.
narration.hi: आख़िरी अलमारी में नातों के शब्द हैं: पिता, माता, भाई, दाता। स्याही से सना भूत उस पर कूदकर कलम हिलाता है। “ये {{ऋ}} पर समाप्त होते हैं,” दादी कहती हैं। “वह स्वर जो लगभग र है। जहाँ हो सके वह {{अर्}} बन जाता है; और कहीं {{र्}}।” शुक “पिता, माता, भ्राता” बुदबुदाता है मानो लोरी आज़मा रहा हो।

body.en: Words in -{{ऋ}} are mostly kin and agents: {{पितृ}} (father), {{मातृ}} (mother, feminine), {{भ्रातृ}} (brother), {{दातृ}} (giver), {{नेतृ}} (leader). The first singular lengthens to {{आ}}: {{पिता}}, {{माता}}, {{दाता}}.

caption.en: A father, in every case and number
caption.hi: पितृ, हर विभक्ति और वचन में

note.en: {{पिता}}, {{पितरौ}}, {{पितरः}}; then {{पित्रा}} (by), {{पित्रे}} (to), {{पितुः}} (from, of), {{पितरि}} (in). {{पितरौ}} also means “the two parents”.

caption.en: A mother, in every case and number
caption.hi: मातृ, हर विभक्ति और वचन में

note.en: The feminine matches the masculine except in the second plural: {{मातॄः}}, not {{मातॄन्}}.
note.hi: स्त्रीलिंग पुंलिंग जैसा है, सिवाय द्वितीया बहुवचन के: {{मातॄः}}, {{मातॄन्}} नहीं।

caption.en: A giver, first and sixth case

note.en: Add {{तृ}} to a root to say “one who …”: {{दातृ}} from {{दा}}, {{कर्तृ}} from {{कृ}}, {{नेतृ}} from {{नी}}.

prompt.en: Fill in the missing forms of the table.

explain.en: Every form is in the table you just read.
explain.hi: हर रूप उसी तालिका में है जो अभी पढ़ी।

prompt.en: Fill in the missing forms of a feminine in -ऋ.
prompt.hi: -ऋ वाले एक स्त्रीलिंग के छूटे रूप भरिए।

explain.hi: {{मातृ}} {{पितृ}} जैसा चलती है, एक परिवर्तन के साथ।

prompt.en: Join each form to its case and number.
prompt.hi: हर रूप को उसकी विभक्ति और वचन से जोड़िए।

explain.hi: प्रत्यय से पहले {{ऋ}} {{र्}} या {{अर्}} बन जाता है।

prompt.en: Tap every form of {{पितृ}} that has {{अर्}}.
prompt.hi: {{पितृ}} के हर रूप को छुइए जिसमें {{अर्}} है।

success.en: “मातुः,” you say. The mist-figures on the last shelf lean into one another: father, mother, brother, giver, a family. The ink-stained spirit sets down his pen, and for the first time he is not writing. “कविः कवी कवयः,” he recites, a gift. “एकं पत्रम्, द्वे पत्रे, त्रीणि पत्राणि।”
success.hi: “मातुः,” आप कहते हैं। आख़िरी अलमारी की धुंध-आकृतियाँ एक-दूसरे की ओर झुकती हैं: पिता, माता, भाई, दाता, एक परिवार। स्याही से सना भूत अपनी कलम रख देता है, और पहली बार वह लिख नहीं रहा। “कविः कवी कवयः,” वह उपहार के रूप में सुनाता है। “एकं पत्रम्, द्वे पत्रे, त्रीणि पत्राणि।”

failure.en: The figures stay apart. “Of the mother”: the sixth case, {{मातुः}}.
failure.hi: आकृतियाँ अलग रहती हैं। ‘माता का’: षष्ठी, {{मातुः}}।

body.en: Sūtra 7.3.110, {{ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः}}, gives {{ऋ}} its strong form {{अर्}} before {{ङि}} and the strong endings: {{पितरि}}, {{पितरौ}}, {{पितरः}}. Sūtra 7.1.94 makes the first singular {{पिता}} by turning {{ऋ}} into {{अन्}} and lengthening.
body.hi: सूत्र 7.3.110, {{ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः}}, {{ङि}} और बलवान् प्रत्ययों से पहले {{ऋ}} को उसका प्रबल रूप {{अर्}} देता है: {{पितरि}}, {{पितरौ}}, {{पितरः}}। सूत्र 7.1.94 प्रथमा एकवचन {{पिता}} बनाता है, {{ऋ}} को {{अन्}} करके और दीर्घ करके।
